Text:
Silvana was never meant to be famous.

It was a lantern town at the kingdom's edge, a place of rain-slick roofs, warm tavern smoke, and old roads that ended at a sealed dungeon stair.

Then the stair opened.

At first came treasure-seekers, soldiers, scholars, and fools. They entered with bright steel and louder promises. Most did not return.
Those who did come back spoke of relics older than the kingdom, rooms that remembered sins, and guardians bound to principles no living priest could fully name.

Now the town waits in the shadow of the dungeon.

The tavern keeps a candle in the window. The barracks counts missing names. The church prays for heroes it has not met yet.

You arrive with your own reasons.

Fame, duty, coin, grief, curiosity, redemption: whatever brought you here, the dungeon will ask what it is worth.

Silvana has sent out its plea.

Step below, if you choose. Return with answers, if the dark allows it.
'Hello...who's there?'
You see a small child peak out from behind some rubble.
'This place is scary...I want to go home.'
'Can you help me find my way out of here?'
You have found the little boy, Timmy, and escort him home.
A woman rushes past the Sergeant before he can finish thanking you.
Timmy hides behind her coat, still dusty from the dungeon, but alive.
'I told them someone brave would find me,' he says, trying very hard not to cry.
The Sergeant looks away for a moment and clears his throat.
'You did more than complete an assignment today. You brought a family back together.'
A brilliant column of light highlights a small piece of ore resting on the ground at the center of the room.
You approach it with caution but find no traps or tricks.
This must be the legendary ore you have heard so much about...
You reach for it, half expecting to be obliterated...but all you feel is warmth throughout your body.
You have obtained the Unobtainium!
Before you lies the body of a warrior, battered, bloody, and broken.
The crushed locket at his throat bears the same name the Waitress speaks like a prayer: Joffrey.
Whatever choices led him here, the grief waiting above is real.
You move the body for a proper burial and take the locket carefully.
Someone in Silvana deserves the truth, even if the truth cannot make this merciful.
You pile stones over Joffrey and leave the dungeon a little quieter than you found it.
The door to the tavern swings shut and you can no longer hear the waitress fleeing.
Just then you hear the bartender from behind the bar. 'Hey, where are you going?!'
'Damn, now whose gonna get this food and drink out to my patrons?!'
For a heartbeat the tavern feels less like a refuge and more like a room holding its breath.
You shrug your shoulders, not wanting to get caught up in all of the chaos.
'BUSBOY! Get out here, you've gotta take over these tables.'
The Waitress kneels beside the locket as if holding it tightly enough might make it answer.
'Joffrey... no. No, you promised me you would come home.'
Her grief turns toward you, raw enough to become blame before either of you can stop it.
'You found him and still he is gone. Why does everyone get to choose, and I am left with what choice costs?'
She rises shaking, and sorrow becomes violence.
That key that you have...that's one of our storage locker keys.
You say you got this from the waitress at the tavern?
She attacked you?! Grief can break a person in ways no sword should have to answer.
Maybe this key is to his locker. Let me see...yes it is.
All that's left inside are some potions and this letter.
'My love, I know you have questions but the answers will not be to your liking...
forgive me but I could not resist his will. If you are reading this, it means I am dead...
please remember that above all, I love you.' -Joffrey
The Sergeant reads the last line twice, then folds the letter with unusual care.
'Whatever Joffrey meant, he loved her. Do not let the rest of this place make you forget that.'
Keep your wits about you, there's evil afoot.
Since there is no one left to claim his things, you can have what's left. Put them to good use.
You enter into the back of the blacksmith shop and see what looks like a metal coffin glowing green.
'Climb on in, we have some work to do.' You enter the machine against your better judgment.
Griswold stands behind a panel and after a few button presses, you see the green glow around you grow.
You are suddenly overwhelmed by an searing pain. You stifle a scream but it is becoming unbearable.
Just as you think you can't take more, the whir of the machine begins to wane.
Your whole body hurts but strangely you feel a power inside of you that you have never experienced.
'How do you feel? Any different?' You exit the chamber more powerful than you entered it.
The invisible force that once blocked you path is now gone.
What lies ahead is unknown.
Proceed at your own peril...
You enter a massive room where twilight hangs in the air like a second sky.
A pale star burns above the far altar, bright enough to hurt and cold enough to silence the breath in your chest.
The figure waiting beneath it is neither fiend nor king.
'You carried every relic here and still do not understand what they guard,' Vesperion says.
'Choice made every wound you passed on the way to me. Every grief. Every betrayal. Every brave, doomed hope.'
The six relics answer in your pack, but their light feels incomplete.
'If Voluntas is sacred, champion, then choose what its suffering is worth.'
The Evening Star descends.
For one impossible breath you see every choice you ever made arranged in a perfect, merciless pattern.
Vesperion closes his hand, and the pattern breaks.
'You mistake endurance for freedom,' he says. 'Now witness what choice leaves behind.'
You wake on cold stone beneath a sky with no horizon, wounded but alive.
The Liminal Gap stretches around you: neither dungeon nor afterlife, but a gray sanctuary caught between a last breath and the next choice.
A hidden guide speaks from somewhere beyond the veil, voice thin with pain.
'Voluntas is not lost. Not yet. Come to the center, and do not mistake survival for escape.'
The final chamber refuses you.
Twilight gathers along the edge of the door, bright and silent, then hardens into an unseen wall.
The hidden guide's voice returns: 'Not this way. The wound in Voluntas remains unresolved, and Vesperion is waiting for a choice you cannot yet make.'
The Hooded Figure kneels beside a dim white flame, one hand pressed against a wound that bleeds starlight instead of blood.
The same presence that haunted your path now looks smaller, older, and terribly tired.
'Yes,' the figure says. 'I guided you. I frightened you. I withheld more than I should have.'
'But Vesperion has thrown you where his mercy cannot fully reach. Here, in the Liminal Gap, the forgotten principle still has an echo.'
'I am not your enemy. Not anymore, if I ever was.'
The Hooded Figure lays a trembling hand over the dim flame.
Your name briefly appears inside it, written in light that refuses to hold still.
'This is not safety,' the guide says. 'It is only an anchor. But for now, an anchor is enough.'
The Hooded Figure turns toward the six sealed paths.
'Voluntas is not a thing I can hand you,' the guide says. 'It is a pattern you must recognize.'
'Tell me which Guardians have answered, and I will help you hear what their answers mean together.'
The torn threshold shivers when you approach, showing the final chamber for less than a heartbeat.
Then the vision folds shut.
The Hooded Figure's voice follows softly: 'Vesperion broke the road behind you. The way back must be earned through the Guardians he tried to make the world forget.'
Three pale lines form a triangle in the air, each side trembling as if it might become a different shape.
A voice without a mouth asks, 'What remains when name, body, and memory disagree?'
The gate of Triangulus waits for the trial of Self.
The triangle opens without moving.
Three versions of your shadow step away from you: one wearing your name, one carrying your wounds, and one made from every remembered choice.
The voice asks again, softer now: 'What proves that you are not merely what happened to you?'
You speak your name and the path you chose to walk.
The shadow wearing your name bows, not because a name is enough, but because a chosen name can become a vow.
The first side of the triangle steadies.
You answer with the body that endured: hunger, wounds, fear, strength, weakness, and every step that still moved forward.
The wounded shadow places a hand over its heart and becomes your own shape again.
The second side of the triangle steadies.
You answer with memory: not perfect, not painless, but yours.
The shadow of remembered choices opens its hands, and the choices remain choices instead of chains.
The third side of the triangle steadies.
The three sides meet and hold.
A small light appears where they join, neither relic nor command.
For a moment, you understand the first fragment of Voluntas: selfhood is not assigned. It is chosen, answered, and chosen again.
The three shadows close over you, not as executioners, but as questions you cannot yet answer.
Name, body, and memory scatter like loose pages.
You wake in the Liminal Gap with the trial still waiting.
Four right angles burn into the stone, perfect and pitiless.
Every step near the gate feels counted before you take it.
The gate of Quadrata waits for the trial of Order.
The square opens into a room of measured paths.
Every stone waits for a rule, and every rule waits for someone to mistake obedience for meaning.
A voice asks, 'When order becomes a prison, what gives it purpose?'
You walk the pattern exactly as given.
The room accepts the discipline of restraint, but not as surrender.
Order steadies when chosen with open eyes.
You step against the count, and the square shakes around you.
The walls do not fall. Instead, they make room for dissent.
Order survives when it can be questioned without breaking.
You trace a new line through the old geometry.
The rule changes, not into chaos, but into a shape that can shelter more than one path.
Order becomes strongest when it can be remade by those who live inside it.
The four angles soften but do not collapse.
A second light joins the first clue of Voluntas.
You understand that law without choice is only a cage.
A six-sided sign of root, wing, tooth, tide, stone, and breath turns slowly above the path.
The air smells of rain on soil that has never known a sun.
The gate of Hexagonum waits for the trial of Nature.
The hexagon opens into a living hush.
Roots cross old bones, water moves under stone, and unseen wings stir the gray air.
A voice asks, 'When life hungers, shelters, flees, and grows, where does will begin?'
You kneel beside the roots and choose to remain.
The ground accepts patience as a living answer.
To be natural is not only to move. Sometimes it is to belong.
You bare your resolve like a fang.
The wild dark does not shame survival.
To be natural is to defend the life that still chooses to live.
You follow the hidden water instead of forcing the stone aside.
The path bends, and bending becomes motion.
To be natural is to change without becoming empty.
The six signs turn once and settle.
A third light wakes beside the others.
You understand that instinct can begin a path, but choice decides what it means.
Moonlight gathers in a silver arch, gentle enough to comfort and sharp enough to wound.
Something beyond it waits with open hands.
The gate of Luna waits for the trial of Love.
The moonlit arch opens on a room where every echo sounds like someone you once failed.
A fragile light rests between your hands, warm and terribly easy to crush.
A voice asks, 'What is love when mercy can wound as deeply as cruelty?'
You close your hands around the fragile light and shield it from the cold.
The moon does not ask whether protection is easy.
Love becomes a promise to guard what cannot guard itself.
You open your hands and let the fragile light rise.
It trembles, then steadies beyond your reach.
Love becomes trust when holding on would only make a cage.
You let the fragile light divide between your palms and the waiting dark.
Neither half fades.
Love becomes choice when it gives without disappearing.
The moonlit arch dims to a gentle silver line.
A fourth light joins the growing pattern.
You understand that love without choice is possession, duty, or fear, but not love.
A single fixed star shines above the gate, unmoving while the whole Liminal sky drifts around it.
For a moment you know exactly where to go, then forget why.
The gate of Polaris waits for the trial of Guidance.
The fixed star lowers until it hangs at eye level.
Three paths appear beneath it: one lit, one dark, and one marked by footprints that are not yours.
A voice asks, 'When guidance points the way, what keeps it from becoming command?'
You follow the lit path.
The star does not drag you forward. It simply remains where it promised to be.
Guidance becomes grace when trust is freely given.
You stop beneath the star and ask why.
The light brightens, not offended by your doubt.
Guidance becomes wisdom when it can answer a living mind.
You follow the footprints only until memory warns you they are not your own.
Then you turn by what you have learned.
Guidance becomes yours when it helps you choose, not vanish.
The fixed star returns to the impossible sky.
A fifth light appears in the pattern.
You understand that a guide can show a road, but Voluntas is the step you take yourself.
The path beyond the gate appears to turn back into itself forever.
Each echo of your breath arrives a little later than the last.
The gate of Infinitas waits for the trial of Eternity.
The path opens and repeats: the same stone, the same breath, the same ache in your bones.
A thousand versions of you keep walking because stopping feels like failure.
A voice asks, 'What gives endurance meaning when the struggle has no end?'
You keep walking.
The endless path recognizes courage in persistence.
Endurance becomes will when each step is chosen again.
You refuse the next repeated step.
The loop cracks, not because you were stronger than eternity, but because you saw the pattern.
Endurance becomes will when it can choose a different shape.
You sit down in the middle of forever.
The path waits, and waiting does not destroy you.
Endurance becomes will when rest is chosen instead of stolen.
The repeated path falls silent.
A sixth light joins the others, and the pattern nearly speaks.
You understand that eternity without choice is only repetition.
The repeated path folds over you until every step feels borrowed from the one before it.
For a moment, continuing and surrendering become indistinguishable.
You wake in the Liminal Gap with one more chance to choose the next step.
The triangle opens again, deeper than the first question.
Name, body, and memory stand apart like three witnesses, each true and each incomplete.
The self will not be owned by any single proof.
Your name answers first, not as a label given by the world, but as a vow you choose to keep.
The other witnesses remain beside it. A name can guide the self, but it cannot imprison it.
Your body answers with every scar, hunger, breath, and step that carried you here.
The other witnesses do not vanish. Flesh remembers the path, but it does not own the whole soul.
Memory answers with broken light: grief, triumph, shame, mercy, and choices still changing shape.
The other witnesses hold steady. What you remember can shape you, but it cannot finish you.
The square descends into a court of rules carved before any living voice could consent.
Every command is clean. Every path is safe. Every silence is mistaken for peace.
Order waits to learn whether it can be worthy of the people inside it.
You obey, but not because the rule owns you.
Chosen discipline gives the square dignity. Order becomes shelter only while consent remains alive.
You resist, and the square does not collapse.
A rule that cannot survive refusal was never order. It was fear wearing symmetry.
You rewrite the path, and the old angles make room for a living hand.
Order becomes worthy when those bound by it can change it without being destroyed.
The hexagon opens into root, fang, and river, three impulses moving before thought can name them.
Nature offers belonging, survival, and change.
Meaning begins when instinct becomes a chosen answer.
You choose the root and feel patience reach down into dark soil.
Belonging becomes more than habit when you decide what will be nourished there.
You choose the fang and let survival show its honest edge.
Defense becomes more than hunger when it protects a life still capable of mercy.
You choose the river and let motion teach the stone a gentler language.
Change becomes more than flight when it carries meaning forward.
The moon hangs close enough to touch, and every silver beam looks like an open hand.
Love offers protection, release, and sharing, each with its own wound.
The trial asks whether care can remain care without becoming possession.
You choose to protect, and the moonlight gathers around what is fragile.
Protection becomes love only when it guards freedom instead of replacing it.
You choose to release, and the moonlight rises beyond the reach of your hands.
Letting go becomes love when trust remains after control is surrendered.
You choose to share, and the moonlight divides without diminishing.
Giving becomes love when neither soul is erased by the gift.
The fixed star lowers until its light becomes a question instead of a command.
One path asks for trust, one for doubt, and one for memory.
Guidance must leave room for the guided to remain alive.
You choose trust, and the star holds steady without pulling you forward.
Guidance becomes grace when the next step is invited, not seized.
You choose to question, and the star brightens instead of punishing the doubt.
Guidance becomes wisdom when it can answer without demanding worship.
You choose to remember, and old directions return as tools instead of chains.
Guidance becomes yours when it helps you find north after the light is gone.
The endless path opens beneath a sky that repeats the same gray breath forever.
Continuing, breaking, and resting each stand before you as real choices.
Endurance is meaningful only while the next step remains yours.
You choose to endure, and the repeated stones become steps instead of chains.
Continuing becomes will when each motion is chosen again.
You choose to break the loop, and eternity admits it was never the only shape.
Refusal becomes endurance when it protects the soul from empty repetition.
You choose to rest, and forever waits without devouring you.
Rest becomes endurance when stopping is chosen before the self is spent.
The Hooded Figure draws six marks in the ash-gray air.
Some burn brighter now, carrying not only answers but the depth beneath them.
The trials do not demand a new path. They ask you to remember why the chosen one matters.
The six lights answer one another across the Liminal Gap.
Self, Order, Nature, Love, Guidance, and Eternity form a shape with one wound at its center.
The Hooded Figure whispers, 'Now you can see what history forgot. Go to the empty Seventh Seat.'
The empty seat waits in perfect silence.
Six marks circle it, but some remain dark.
Whatever belongs here will not answer until every Guardian clue has awakened.
The empty Seventh Seat does not fill.
No relic appears. No crown descends. No hidden weapon waits in the gray light.
Instead, the six awakened clues bend toward the absence and name what was removed.
Voluntas: the choice that gives every other principle meaning.
Vesperion once guarded this seat. Then he hollowed it from history because he mistook peace for silence.
The Hooded Figure lowers their gaze before the empty seat.
'I am not Voluntas,' they say. 'I am only one of its witnesses, wounded and left behind when Vesperion broke the road.'
'I preserved enough of the path for one soul to choose it again. That must be you, if you can face every self you did not become.'
The Acolyte kneels with their face turned away from the empty seat.
They do not threaten you.
They only whisper, 'You still think there is something here to find. There is only pain wearing a nobler name.'
The Acolyte looks up, and for a moment you see the outline of someone who once stood where you stand.
'I chose until choosing broke me,' they say. 'Vesperion offered mercy. No more wrong turns. No more grief born from my own hand.'
'At first it felt like peace. Then I understood: a life without choice can no longer wound, but it can no longer love either.'
They turn back toward the gray light. 'Go on, then. Prove your burden means something.'
The Hooded Figure studies the Class Ring without reaching for it.
'Voluntas does not ask you to become every possible self,' they say.
'It asks whether the self you brought here was chosen freely enough to stand before the dark.'
The Class Ring remains quiet, its promise still unawakened.
Even dormant, it holds the shape of a path: not power owed, but identity carried.
The Hooded Figure nods. 'A path can be true before it is complete.'
The Class Ring answers with a pulse of remembered trial.
Its awakened mark does not command you forward. It bears witness to a choice already made and kept.
The Hooded Figure lowers their head. 'Then let that choice stand among the others.'
The ring remembers discipline: hands that rose again, wounds carried without surrender, strength chosen instead of commanded.
'Then let your strength remain yours,' the Hooded Figure says.
The ring remembers study, prayer, stars, and the terrible patience of power held back by will.
'Then let knowledge answer choice, not replace it,' the Hooded Figure says.
The ring remembers crossed roads: blade and vow, trick and truth, law and mercy held in one imperfect hand.
'Then let the mixed path stand without apology,' the Hooded Figure says.
The ring remembers bonds: songs, summons, packs, and every promise that still leaves room for another soul to answer.
'Then let fellowship remain chosen, not owned,' the Hooded Figure says.
The ring remembers hidden roads: debt, stealth, hunger, masks, and the stubborn refusal to let darkness choose your name.
'Then let even the shadow belong to the one who walks it,' the Hooded Figure says.
The ring remembers no old category clearly enough to name you.
That, too, is a kind of freedom.
'Then let the unrecorded path be yours,' the Hooded Figure says.
The Hooded Figure gestures toward the Class Ring's remembered light.
'A path does not become true because it was painless,' they say.
'It becomes true because you keep choosing it after seeing what else might have been.'
The ring answers with the weight of held ground and wounds that did not become masters.
Strength remains Voluntas when it protects the hand that chooses how to use it.
The ring answers with patient formulae, prayers, and stars that never mistook knowledge for command.
Power remains Voluntas when wisdom leaves room for refusal.
The ring answers from the crossing of several roads, none clean enough to own the whole truth.
A mixed path remains Voluntas when every part of it is still freely carried.
The ring answers with the warmth of chosen bonds: summons, songs, packs, and promises that can answer back.
Fellowship remains Voluntas when love does not become possession.
The ring answers from hidden roads, where hunger and secrecy could have become chains.
Shadow remains Voluntas when even the dark is made to answer the one who walks it.
The ring answers without a clean category.
The Hooded Figure almost smiles. 'Then let the unwritten road remain written by your steps.'
The Hooded Figure turns the Class Ring toward the empty seventh place.
'Every class is a way of answering pressure,' they say. 'Let yours answer without becoming a command.'
Weapon forms move through the ring like remembered stances, each one chosen and refined by use.
Voluntas holds where mastery remains a discipline, not a cage.
Contract marks glow and fade around the ring, bargains named instead of hidden.
Voluntas holds where even dangerous pacts are faced as choices with costs.
Venom, stone, growth, and storm turn in the ring without drowning one another.
Voluntas holds where balance is tended, not imposed.
Old scars burn red around the ring, but none of them speak in your place.
Voluntas holds where fury remains answerable to the one who survives it.
The vow in the ring brightens like a road walked under witness.
Voluntas holds where oath and mercy can still be chosen together.
The ring remembers the height before the fall and the will that chooses when to land.
Voluntas holds where courage leaps without becoming escape.
A shield-line forms in the ring, not as a wall against life but as a promise kept.
Voluntas holds where protection remains freely given.
Six schools turn in the ring like answers that could have become laws.
Voluntas holds where knowledge serves choice instead of replacing it.
Umbral debt gathers in the ring and stops just short of naming you.
Voluntas holds where shadow is carried openly enough to be refused.
Steel and spell meet in the ring, neither one allowed to erase the other.
Voluntas holds where a divided art becomes a chosen rhythm.
Xenid names echo through the ring as bonds, not possessions.
Voluntas holds where command remains partnership.
Chance flickers in the ring like a loaded die set down before it is thrown.
Voluntas holds where luck bends, but does not decide, the hand.
Case notes, maps, and hidden caches arrange themselves around the ring.
Voluntas holds where truth opens roads instead of closing them.
A no-trace path crosses the ring and leaves only the choice to step from shadow.
Voluntas holds where silence does not become surrender.
Stolen sparks glimmer in the ring, transformed by wit rather than ownership.
Voluntas holds where theft becomes responsibility for what is carried.
Ordered blessings pass through the ring in a measured procession.
Voluntas holds where faith protects without demanding obedience.
Staff-light and shield-shadow cross inside the ring without forcing one another aside.
Voluntas holds where devotion becomes a chosen channel, not a hand closing around the self.
Ki settles in the ring like breath returning after a strike.
Voluntas holds where discipline makes room for stillness.
Prayer gathers in the ring as a vigil that does not bargain for control.
Voluntas holds where mercy answers suffering without owning it.
A final refrain moves through the ring, softer than command and harder to silence.
Voluntas holds where a song can end and still leave choice behind.
Moonlight and hunger circle the ring, answered by a name that stays human enough to choose.
Voluntas holds where instinct is met, not erased.
Constellations turn inside the ring, each sign bright enough to guide and dim enough to refuse.
Voluntas holds where fate is read without being obeyed.
Totem aspects gather at the ring's edge, ancestral voices waiting for consent.
Voluntas holds where the dead are honored without being used as chains.
A companion's heartbeat answers beside the ring, close but never owned.
Voluntas holds where loyalty can still answer back.
The ring cannot name the class path cleanly, but it still keeps the shape of a chosen road.
Voluntas holds where even an old or unrecorded self remains free to answer.
As the Reflection gathers, the Class Ring answers the empty seventh place.
Not as a weapon. Not as proof of worth.
Only as a quiet echo that this path is yours because you chose it.
The mirror-dark threshold ripples, but no image holds.
A thousand possible selves wait beyond it, silent and unfinished.
The path will not open until Voluntas is remembered and the Acolyte's warning has been faced.
The threshold becomes a mirror, and the mirror becomes a crowd.
You see every path not taken: every class you did not become, every mercy withheld or granted, every weapon set down or raised.
The Reflection does not ask which life was correct.
It asks whether the life you chose is truly yours.
The threshold becomes a mirror polished by blade marks and old bruises.
Every path not taken watches from behind raised steel.
The Reflection does not ask whether strength was the only answer.
It asks whether the strength you chose still belongs to you.
The threshold becomes a mirror filled with unwritten sigils and prayers you never learned.
Every path not taken speaks in a voice almost like your own.
The Reflection does not ask whether wisdom should have spared you pain.
It asks whether the power you chose can remain a choice.
The threshold becomes a mirror of crossed roads.
Steel, spell, mercy, fear, and stubborn hope move through it in a crowd of almost-selves.
The Reflection does not ask which path was pure.
It asks whether the mixed life you chose is truly yours.
You claim this path without pretending it was the only possible road.
The mirror accepts the answer: a chosen life does not need to erase its alternatives.
You carry the untaken roads as memory, not command.
The mirror accepts the answer: regret can be honored without being obeyed.
You answer that choosing is not finished because one choice was made.
The mirror accepts the answer: Voluntas lives wherever the next free step remains possible.
The mirror remembers your answer.
It does not ask you to improve it. It asks whether you can still stand behind it.
Your answer returns from the glass with its edges no longer shaking.
The possible selves fall quiet because the chosen self has spoken freely.
The mirror widens until it holds more than your face.
Guardian answers, class vows, ring-light, regret, and refusal gather in one impossible reflection.
The Reflection does not weigh them as proof. It asks whether you can recognize them as yours.
The path shown in the mirror does not become simpler after victory.
It becomes yours without apology.
Voluntas answers from every step you chose and every step you refused.
The possible selves fall quiet.
They do not vanish in defeat. They bow to the one path that is real because you chose it.
Voluntas flares in the empty place where command once stood.
The way back opens.
The martial shadows lower their weapons.
They do not vanish in defeat. They recognize the discipline you kept choosing when fear wanted command.
Voluntas flares through the stance that remains yours.
The way back opens.
The unwritten voices fall silent.
They do not vanish in defeat. They recognize the knowledge you chose without letting it choose for you.
Voluntas flares through the spell that remains yours.
The way back opens.
The crossed roads settle into one living path.
They do not vanish in defeat. They recognize every imperfect answer you carried forward.
Voluntas flares through the life that remains yours.
The way back opens.
The mirror-dark threshold cracks across your vision.
The possible selves do not condemn you. They simply wait.
You wake again in the Liminal Gap, wounded but still capable of choosing.
The raised blades turn aside your answer before it can hold.
The martial shadows do not condemn you. They simply wait.
You wake again in the Liminal Gap, wounded but still capable of choosing.
The unwritten voices drown your answer before it can hold.
The mystic shadows do not condemn you. They simply wait.
You wake again in the Liminal Gap, wounded but still capable of choosing.
The crossed roads split beneath your feet before your answer can hold.
The almost-selves do not condemn you. They simply wait.
You wake again in the Liminal Gap, wounded but still capable of choosing.
The Hooded Figure lifts their head as the Reflection falls silent.
For one breath the hood cannot hide the light beneath it: not command, not judgment, but witness.
'I was made to remember what Vesperion tried to make mercifully forgotten,' they say.
'No name I give you matters more than the choice you just proved. Go back as yourself.'
The Hooded Figure keeps their hood drawn even now.
'A name would turn the witness into the answer,' they say. 'I am not the answer.'
'I kept a door from closing. You chose to walk through it. That is enough.'
The torn threshold unfolds.
Beyond it waits the final chamber, not as memory and not as dream.
The Hooded Figure steadies the dim flame one last time. 'Go back. This time, Vesperion cannot choose for you.'
The final chamber recognizes you differently now.
Vesperion turns beneath the Evening Star, and the face behind the busboy's borrowed kindness is no longer hidden.
'You found the wound I spared the world from naming,' he says.
'Look at Joffrey. Look at the Waitress. Look at every ruin choice left behind. Tell me again that Voluntas is mercy.'
The six relics answer, incomplete no longer.
You step forward with every choice that made you.
Vesperion studies the path that followed you back from the Liminal Gap.
'You call it freedom because you survived long enough to name it,' he says.
'But every answer you carry is another wound you were forced to make meaningful.'
'The tavern boy smiled because it was useful,' Vesperion says, and the borrowed gentleness is gone.
'Joffrey died. The Waitress broke. You watched grief become another proof you could not bear to surrender.'
'I did not invent pain. I offered the only mercy that would have ended its need for permission.'
The Evening Star fractures without falling.
Vesperion reaches for the pattern one last time, but the six awakened principles refuse to close around your will.
For the first time, his mercy has no command inside it.
'Then choose,' he whispers, no longer triumphant. 'Choose all of it. Even the pain.'
The light breaks, and the hollow where Voluntas was erased begins to remember its own name.
The final chamber does not crown you. It opens.
You do not take Voluntas. You leave it free.
The Liminal Gap exhales through the world.
Self, Order, Nature, Love, Guidance, and Eternity remain, but none of them stand alone anymore.
Voluntas is not restored as a relic or throne. It returns wherever a soul can answer yes, no, stay, go, forgive, refuse, begin again.
The grief Vesperion used does not vanish. Joffrey is still gone. The Waitress still suffered. The Acolyte still chose peace until peace became empty.
But grief is no longer proof that choice should be buried.
The Hooded Figure watches from the threshold as dawn reaches places twilight tried to keep.
The Forsaken Tenet is remembered.
For a moment, memory returns to the tavern where so many choices first tangled.
The bar is quieter now. One table remains unset, and no busboy comes to clear it.
No miracle gives Joffrey back to the Waitress, and no ending makes grief harmless.
Some patrons speak more softly. Some do not speak at all. The ordinary work of cups, chairs, and surviving continues.
But the silence is no longer command. It is a place where the living may choose what to do with love, loss, and morning.
A bright column of light highlights a pedestal at the center of the room.
The object resting there feels older than the chamber around it, important in a way you cannot yet name.
You take the relic and instantly feel rejuvenated.
You have obtained a relic!
Who's there?! Oh, you're not a monster...
You are one of the first travelers I have seen in some time.
I have built up a cache of items that I can sell you if you're interested...
Hello, my name is Chisolm, Griswold's brother.
I tried to defeat the ultimate evil but could not even damage it.
I barely escaped, camping here to lick my wounds.
I decided I would instead use my blacksmith skills to help those who look to do what I could not.
Choose the type of armor you would prefer and I will make you the finest set you could imagine.
Before you sits a decent sized boulder, although you are not sure what it is doing in the dungeon.
You look closer and notice the hilt of a sword sticking out from behind it.
You grab the sword and try to dislodge it but it seems pretty stuck.
With one final yank, the sword comes free...or part of it at least.
You gain the not-so-legendary Excaliper...whomp whomp...
A beautiful maiden emerges from the spring. 'I am Nimue, Maid of this water.'
She senses something in your possession. 'You carry a broken sword...Merzhin's handiwork, no doubt.
That wizard has become a thorn in my side. He resides in the Realm of Cambion.
I can offer you passage there to defeat him, if you prove yourself worthy.
In the meantime, I will take this piece of the sword. It is a poor substitute for the real thing but it will do for now.
If you wish to summon me again, drink from the spring. But first...reconsider your path.'
She vanishes into the water.
Nimue rests a hand on the spring and the water finally settles.
'For years Merzhin bent that realm around my name, making every path a mockery of the lake I guard.'
'You broke more than his body. You broke the shape of his lie.'
For a moment, the reflected stars in the spring arrange themselves into a clear road downward.
'The dungeon will not thank you, champion, but the water remembers. So will I.'
As you enter the corridor, you are met with a horrific scene.
The carnage is almost as unbelievable as the monster you are confronted with.
You first notice the glint of a battle-worn axe, stained with the blood of countless foes.
The beast's fiery eyes lock onto you, letting out a deafening roar.
There is no mistaking the towering Minotaur, known to many as 'The Butcher'.
Chains and bone fragments litter the floor—a grim testament to those who dared to challenge him.
The Butcher snarls, 'You are next, little one!'
The sacred chamber hums with an ominous energy as you step forward, the air growing cold with each breath.
A deep growl reverberates through the hall, and from the shadows emerges a large wolf-like beast.
This must be the Barghest from the Sergeant's reports, a tricky shapeshifter guarding whatever rests in this sealed chamber.
Its spectral eyes burn with a ghostly light, and its jagged fangs gleam with menace.
Its black fur bristles like shadowy flames and its claws carve furrows into the stone floor as it prowls.
With a chilling snarl, it lunges, its voice echoing, “None shall desecrate the altar!”
The dungeon narrows as you round the corner and you are met by a faint, red light.
A warmth meets your body and the sweet smell of jasmine permeates around you.
'Oh please, enter my chamber without permission.' You see nothing but a lavish lair and a crackling fireplace.
You step forward in defiance, spotting the creature perched upon the hearth, no larger than a house cat.
'So, you thought you would make a name for yourself by slaying a mighty dragon? Sorry to disappoint...'
It is true, you did expect something more. However, your experience tells you not to take it lightly.
'Oh, still a bit frisky, are we? Well, I should warn you that short doesn't always mean sweet.'
'But that is enough foreplay, let us proceed to the main course!' The beast takes flight and attacks!
You travel a great hall, expecting something monstrous to attack. What you find is much worse.
The hair on the back of your neck stands at attention and suddenly feel fear grab ahold of you.
Your will is steadfast but you know that will only last for so long as the sight you feared emerges.
A massive stallion with a mane and tail of flames, the rest as black as the deepest depths.
It says no words but has no need, for silence is much more frightening.
You catch a glimpse of a relic perched atop a glowing pedestal but the Nightmare stands in your way.
With a flare of its nostrils, the beast charges right at you, filled with malice aforethought.
As you step into the dimly lit cavern, the air grows thick and heavy.
A low, menacing hiss reverberates off the stone walls, sending shivers down your spine.
A monstrosity emerges from the shadows, its leathery wings unfurling, and its beady eyes locked onto you.
With every movement, its claws scrape against the floor, and its serpentine tail lashes out.
The beast lets out a bone-chilling screech, its petrifying aura threatening to halt your advance.
The stagnant isolation of the dungeon is suddenly disturbed, replaced by a bone-chilling cold.
The icy winds howl as you approach the sacred grounds of the third relic.
Emerging from the darkness, a beast towers above, its gaunt frame shrouded in frost and shadows.
Its hollow eyes burn with a ravenous hunger, and its clawed hands twitch with restless energy.
The air grows colder, biting at your skin, as the creature lets out an unearthly wail.
The guardian of the relic stands ready, an embodiment of hunger and despair, the Wendigo.
The ground trembles as a towering figure of stone and metal lumbers into view.
Its massive frame glints in the dim light, its eyes dead and lifeless.
You stand still waiting for something to happen and notice a low hum build as the construct comes online.
The golem's glowing eyes fixate on you, while the hum of ancient magic reverberates through the air.
Cracks in its surface reveal faint pulsations of energy, hinting at the immense power contained within.
The guardian moves with deliberate purpose, its heavy footsteps echoing like a drumbeat of inevitability.
Another trial stands before you, as implacable as the earth itself.
The Iron Golem stands motionless at the threshold, its massive form forged from enchanted steel.
Etched with ancient runes of power, the massive statue is a formidable sight.
Sparks crackle from its joints as it animates, each movement deliberate and heavy with menace.
Its glowing core pulses like a molten heart, radiating an oppressive heat that fills the chamber.
The ground shudders under its iron steps, and its piercing gaze locks onto you, assessing your worth.
The path forward lies in proving yourself against this unyielding sentinel of the dungeon depths.
You step into the chamber and the carnival noise dies all at once, as if the room itself is holding its breath.
At the center stands the Jester, waiting beneath a wash of impossible color and shifting light.
His costume is immaculate in some places and ruined in others, velvet and bells stitched together with blood-dark thread.
He tilts his head as though studying you, a smile curling slowly across his painted face.
With a flick of the wrist he produces a token, lets it dance across his knuckles, then closes his hand around it.
'You made it through the mirrors,' he says softly. 'Most only find themselves.'
The bells at his cuffs give a faint, deliberate chime as he takes a step forward.
'But every game has rules, and every guest must choose what they are willing to lose.'
His grin widens, equal parts delight and menace, and the chamber seems to bend around him like a stage awaiting its cue.
'Come then,' he says. 'Let us see which face of mine breaks you first.'
Your search for another one of the mystical relics leads you down a dark flight of stairs.
As you descend into the dungeon, you notice the air grow heavy, and a gurgling sound echoing from beyond.
A cartoonish creature emerges, its writhing tentacles glowing faintly with an unearthly, pulsating light.
Its bulbous body quivers, and its eyes...far too many eyes...unnervingly fixate on you.
'You dare face the perfection of creation?' a voice reverberates in your mind. How?!
The creature's tentacles twitch, ready to unleash its magical fury. 'Prepare to witness true power!'
After several minutes exploring an empty corridor, you exit into a massive sanctum riddled with fissures.
The cavern trembles as the ground beneath you grows unbearably hot.
A deafening roar erupts from the shadows, and the Red Dragon steps forward.
Its scales gleam like molten metal and its eyes burn with a primal fury, but something older than rage moves beneath the heat.
'You've come this far,' it growls, its voice reverberating like thunder.
'But you will go no further. Prove your worth... or be reduced to ashes where you stand.'
Its wings spread wide, blocking your path. Whatever truths the dragon carries, this battle will decide whether the road below opens.
You step out from the hidden passage and expect a moment to gather yourself. You were mistaken.
The ground quakes, and an ominous growl fills the air as the three-headed Cerberus emerges before you.
Each head snarls and gnashes in unison, its glowing eyes locking onto you with predatory intent.
'You dare to disturb the sanctity of the final relic?' the voices echo, a guttural chorus of menace.
'No one passes. No one escapes.' The beast's claws dig into the ground, its teeth gleaming in the faint light.
This is your pentultimate test-face the guardian or perish in its jaws.
You feel your body lifted in the air, riding an invisible path toward the far side of the sanctum.
The ride comes to an immediate end, leaving you reeling from the abrupt stop.
The bones of those who have faced the prime evil surround you. Will you join them?
Your thoughts are interrupted by the shaking of the ground as an incomprehesible sight approaches you.
Before you stands the Devil—a towering figure of malice, wreathed in flame and shadow.
Its horns scrape the heavens, and its crimson eyes burn with the fury of eons.
'You may not recognize me in my current form. Let me refresh your memory.'
From the shadows appears the hooded figure from the town tavern.
'You probably expected my appearance but the surprises are just beginning.'
You were certain of their duplicity but your suspicion was only partially correct.
The Devil begins to transform, replacing the monstrosity with a familiar sight-the busboy!
'Not who you expected? I guess you weren't actually paying attention then.'
Your mind races, combing over everything that has happened, certain you have missed some clue.
'I have been lurking, with my trusted acolyte by my side. I knew eventually a worthy opponent would appear.'
A fury rises within you at the thought of all the lives ruined. You clench as he continues to speak.
'I stayed away at first but your success piqued my curiosity. You have earned a mighty reward.'
Reward?! This must be a joke, surely there is nothing left but a battle to the death.
'Join my army and I will make you one of my chosen. You will lead droves of my minions into battle.'
You cry out for silence, insulted by the implication. You would never join him!
'I thought it was a fair offer but so be it. Instead your soul will be used for my amusement.'
The Devil transforms back into his real form and a battle for the ages commences.
The ground feels different here, almost like sand.
Suddenly your whole body starts to shake and the ground starts to open underneath you.
You stumble back just in time and out of the floor a massive earthworm-like creature appears.
'Who dares disturb my home! Give me one reason I shouldn't swallow you right up?'
The game piece you found begins to glows and levitates up into the air.
'Oh look, that will complete my set. Maybe instead of violence, we could help each other out.'
'Give it to me and I will lend you my services when needed.'
You have gained the summon Dilong.
The wails of anguish have settled and the Wendigo lays at your feet.
After a long fight, you take a moment to catch your breath and feel an icy chill creep over you.
A mist has fallen upon the room with an icy film caked over every surface, including you.
A massive shiver runs through your bones and you buckle at your knees in pain.
'I expected more from the one who defeated this beast. Hahaha...pathetic.'
You regain your composure and return to your feet, defiant in the face of the unseen.
An entity forms in front of you with a crooked smile, 'Maybe you are worth something. We shall see...'
You have gained the summon Agloolik.
The searing pain continues as you traverse the blazing hallway, unsure if the reward is worth the pain.
You encounter what appears to be a dead end but notice a pool of lava, bubbling and spitting molten rock.
This must be the place...perhaps there is a way to awaken what dwells here.
You cast the blacksmith's hammer into the lava...and nothing...for a time.
Suddenly a large figure emerges, a man over nine feet tall, engulfed in fire and brimstone.
'I have slumbered for too long. What is this that returns me to the realm of the living?'
'A summoner? Of course, I should have known...the downfalls of my curse. Shall we leave?'
You have gained the summon Cacus.
You drank water from the underground spring...nothing seems to have changed...at first.
Suddenly an eddy forms and out from the vortex emerges a blond-haired maiden in a green silk dress.
A haunting voice echoes around you, even though her mouth does not move.
You start to feel a strange calm, as if you are being lulled to sleep. Is this some kind of trick?
Your question is immediately answered, when the figure changes into something out of the horrors.
An ugly creature, with giant teeth and webbed hands and feet, let's out a shriek and falls to all fours.
As if by some godly power, the creature crawls along the top of the water, heading right toward you.
You are overcome with an almost mystical level of fear, frozen in place even against your will.
Giant claws reach out for you, no doubt to pull you under. Your resolve finally returns.
You prepare for combat, sure of a fight to ensue.
The Fuath relents slumping to the ground. The creature returns to its original form.
After a moment, you hear a raspy voice coming from inside your head.
'It's been some time since anyone could hold their own against me. Many have tried but none have succeeded.'
Exhaustion is replaced by an expression of hatred. 'I will not submit to your will!'
The Fuath tries to slip back into the waters but is held back by an invisible force.
'NO, I WON'T GO WITH THEM!!!', as if pleading with the universe. The struggle ends quickly.
'CURSES!...I must fulfill the covenant and aid you in your quest...'
You have gained the summon Fuath.
You follow the priest down a dark alley, passing several homeless people before arriving at a tent.
'Go inside and tell her I sent you.' The priest turns around and heads back toward the church.
You enter the tent and are instantly hit by a strange odor, not bad but also not good.
A figure emerges from behind a bookshelf. 'Come in, I've been expecting you.'
A masked figure stands before you, minimally clothed in rags and adorned in shells and bones.
'The priest told me you helped the church out immensely. I owe him my life.'
'Perhaps I can help you. You possess the power to summon creatures, a gift not many have mastered.'
From a back room, you hear a bird shriek, followed by a bright flash and the crack of thunder.
'Right on cue, come out Izulu.' To your surprise, a young man emerges from the darkness.
'This is Izulu, my familiar. Don't let this form fool you, my pet is a powerful force.'
At the snap of a finger, the young man transforms into a giant bird. Electricity crackles around him.
'I grant you permission to summon him and do your bidding, until the day the evil is purged.'
You have gained the summon Izulu.
You have gained the summon Hala.
Seraphim answers the Celestial Calling.
Lamashtu answers the Fiend Calling.
Tiamat answers the Dragon Calling.
You have gained the summon Bardi.
You have gained the summon Kobalos.
The Red Dragon's defeat leaves an echo in the scorched air: not Kaelenon's restored self, but an ancient draconic spirit answering to the name Zahhak.
The pact takes shape around your call.
You have gained the summon Zahhak.
You come to the end of a long corridor and realize the dungeon smells just a little worse than normal.
You spot a mass against the wall and quickly identify the insignia of the town guard.
The body is partially eaten but you believe this must be the recruit the Sergeant told you about.
You retrieve the body that even though is missing parts, still weighs quite a bit.
As you turn to leave you come face to face with the culprits and they attack!
You follow the priest down a dark alley, passing several homeless people before arriving at a tent.
'Go inside and tell her I sent you.' The priest turns around and heads back toward the church.
You enter the tent and are instantly hit by a strange odor, not bad but also not good.
A figure emerges from behind a bookshelf. 'Come in, I've been expecting you.'
A masked figure stands before you, minimally clothed in rags and adorned in shells and bones.
'The priest told me you helped the church out immensely. I owe him my life.'
'As you likely have guessed, I am a shaman. Some would call me a witch doctor...'
'I believe I can help you in your quest to purge this land of evil. Wait here...'
The shaman exits the room through a flap in the back. You wait for some time...
Suddenly a flash of light and a series of bangs exit the back room, followed by a trail of smoke.
The shaman reemerges. 'Here, take these potions. They will cure all status effects.'
'Good luck. I will do what I can from the shadows to help you.'
You notice a strange tile floor out of place surronded by the dirt ground of the dungeon.
You hesitate at first but decide it can't be that bad, can it?
Immediately after stepping on to the tile your reality twists around you...
Colors swirl, geometry bends impossibly, and gravity seems negotiable.
You are teleported to a strange place of deception, where things are not as they seem.
This place thrums with chaotic magical energy. You must navigate carefully.
Defeat the Jester and find your way out of this labyrinth of madness.
With the Jester's final laugh echoing through the carnival, the illusions begin to crack and shatter.
The twisted landscape convulses, reality reasserting itself piece by piece.
The funhouse collapses around you like a house of cards, but you emerge unscathed.
As the last echoes fade, you find yourself back where you started, victorious.
The Jester has been defeated, and the funhouse is no more.
The force field crackles, and the Jester's laughter skips across the mirrored halls.
'Oh, no, no, no... no admittance without the proper fare,' he sings.
'Four little laughs I hid away where greedy hands meet hungry teeth.'
'Open what grins. Slay what bites. Gather my tokens, and perhaps I'll let the curtain rise.'
The Incubus lets out a final, otherworldly scream as your blow strikes true.
Its demonic form wavers, then shatters like glass into shadow and ash.
The oppressive presence lifts. The air grows clear and breathable once more.
You have proven yourself equal to a being of pure malice and cunning.
A sense of accomplishment fills you. Nimue will be pleased with your victory.
You reach out and grasp the Golden Chalice. It is warm to the touch.
As your fingers close around it, the chalice pulses with ancient power.
You feel the blessing of the chalice settle into your very being.
This sacred vessel will grant you the strength needed to face Merzhin himself.
You notice a loose stone in the boulder's crevice and pry it free.
A weathered map lies folded inside, marked with a strange altar symbol.
Most of the ink has faded to near-blank.
Maybe someone in town can help decipher it.
A weary adventurer emerges from the shadows, clutching an ugly sword.
'I knew someone would come... the map is real,' they whisper.
'The ink is hidden. Study the map closely and the altar marks will surface,' they add before slipping away.
Inspect the Chalice Map to reveal the Golden Chalice location.
The ground trembles beneath your feet.
An ancient altar rises from the stone, revealing a gleaming chalice.
The Golden Chalice has revealed itself at last.
